subject: QuantEdge: sustained tail-latency + 503s — path to commercial resolution
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@quantumedge.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ken O'Leary <ken.oleary@quantumedge.io>, Tom Becker <tom.becker@quantumedge.io>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Production impact this morning (latency + 503s) — urgent

Hi Mina,

We saw a sustained tail-latency increase and intermittent 503s across our inference routes between 02:20–06:10 PT this morning. Error rate peaked at ~4.6% and throughput dropped ~28% on our busiest model. This caused several customer-facing jobs to timeout and one downstream pipeline to requeue.

We raised a ticket with your support (#INC-9812) but wanted to loop you in directly — QuantumEdge is extremely sensitive to availability during our year-end retail window. We need a clear remediation path, and an outline of the commercial make-good you will offer (credits or refunds) if this is an SLA breach.

Attached a trimmed usage report and our internal error logs for your reference.

Please confirm receipt and propose next steps and timing for an exec-level conversation.

Thanks,
Samira
Head of Platform Reliability
QuantumEdge

Attachments: quantumedge-usage-report.csv (CSV, 128KB), internal-errors.log (referenced)

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@quantumedge.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact this morning (latency + 503s) — urgent

Samira —

Thanks for the details and the report, we got it. I’m sorry for the disruption during your peak window. I’ve pulled the incident timeline from our side and asked engineering to prioritize a post-mortem.

Immediate plan:
- I opened an incident bridge with our infra team and traced an atypical autoscaler interaction that caused cold-starts and KV-cache misses.
- We’ll share a preliminary root-cause and a hard timeline for mitigation by EOD PT tomorrow.
- Rishi (copied) will lead the commercial dialogue; Marissa is on standby for exec coordination.

Proposed near-term next step: 30-minute exec-bridge tomorrow (2026-11-19) to review impact, proposed fixes, and discuss short-form credits to offset the customer impact. Does 10:00 PT work for your team?

I’ve attached our incident timeline PDF (preliminary) and the usage CSV you sent.

—
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: sla-incident-timeline.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@quantumedge.io>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T13:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact this morning (latency + 503s) — urgent

Samira —

Appreciate the quick flag. We want to get you to a place where QuantumEdge has confidence in us during your peak windows. High-level options we can discuss on the call:

1) Interim credit offer (pro-rated usage-based credit for the impacted hours + one additional week of discounted throughput)
2) Operational remediation commitment: prioritized capacity reservation for the remainder of your retail window + weekly checkpoints
3) Contract amendment option: SLO addendum with an automatic fallback to a higher-tier concurrency during calendar-critical hours (would require term amendment & signatures)

I’ll bring a draft credit proposal to the bridge and a sample addendum for legal. If you prefer, we can share the proposed make-good doc ahead of the call — Marissa can sign off on escalations.

—Rishi
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@quantumedge.io>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T09:58:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact this morning (latency + 503s) — exec bridge at 10:00 PT

Samira / Ken / Tom —

Thank you for making time. Joining today’s 10:00 PT bridge: Lauren (VP, Customer Success), Rishi (AE), Mina (your RM), and me. Agenda: quick incident recap, live questions, proposed commercial resolution, timeline to close.

Call details: Zoom — https://zoom.us/j/999999999 (passcode: QE-Exec)

Notes we’ll cover:
- Estimated impacted tokens & percent of peak throughput (from attached CSV)
- Fault window and root-cause hypothesis (engineering will review)
- Proposed credit structure: 20% credit on impacted usage hours + one month of prioritized capacity at no additional cost (draft attached).
- Contract path: expedited addendum sign-off or one-off credit if you prefer to avoid a change to the contract.

If you have a different remedy in mind please share before the call so we can surface approvals.

—
Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Ken O'Leary <ken.oleary@quantumedge.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@quantumedge.io>, Tom Becker <tom.becker@quantumedge.io>
Date: 2026-11-20T11:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact this morning (latency + 503s) — exec bridge at 10:00 PT

Thanks for the call earlier. QuantumEdge appreciates the responsiveness. A few clarifying points and our preferences:

- The business impact was material — multiple merchant jobs failed and one partner ticket escalated. We estimate direct revenue risk over the next 30 days if this repeats.
- We prefer a contract amendment that includes: (a) guaranteed prioritized capacity during agreed calendar-critical hours; (b) a clear credit formula triggered by threshold breaches (not ad-hoc); (c) incident forensics SLA for post-mortem in 48 hours.
- We reviewed the draft make-good and proposed a redline on the credit percentage and the look-back window (attached DocuSign link).

Ken
CRO, QuantumEdge

Attachments/links: DocuSign proposed addendum (https://www.docusign.com/secure-link/QE-Makegood-v2).

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ken O'Leary <ken.oleary@quantumedge.io>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@quantumedge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact this morning (latency + 503s) — path forward and next steps

Ken / Samira —

Thanks again for the constructive call and the redlines. Internal here — we discussed legal and product tradeoffs and can move quickly on a formal addendum. Proposed next steps:

1) Rishi will send an updated make-good: combines a percentage credit (per your redline) and a single month of prioritized capacity during your identified calendar-critical hours.
2) Product will ship a short-term config change to pin an elevated concurrency profile for your production cluster for the remainder of the retail window — ops will deploy tonight.
3) Marissa & Lauren will coordinate an accelerated legal review; target: signed addendum within 5 business days.
4) We will deliver a 48-hour forensics write-up and a 90-day monitoring playbook.

I attached the revised make-good draft (proposed-makegood-term_v2.docx) and the incident timeline PDF we referenced. If that looks good, Rishi will send the DocuSign link by tomorrow morning.

Action items for QuantumEdge: please confirm the calendar-critical hours you want prioritized and approve the revised credit percentage in the attached doc so we can finalize.

We’re committed to earning back your trust — we’ll also schedule weekly check-ins for the next month.

—
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed-makegood-term_v2.docx
